{"sectionRef":"§ 13.3 Covenants by RevMed. RevMed covenants to Sanofi that:","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0565","text":"13.3 Covenants by RevMed. RevMed covenants to Sanofi that:"},{"id":"p0566","text":"(a) RevMed will not, and will cause its Affiliates not to, grant a lien on the RevMed Licensed Technology to any Third Party or knowingly permit a lien to be imposed on the RevMed Licensed Technology other than those disclosed to Sanofi by RevMed and that do not conflict with the rights granted Sanofi hereunder."},{"id":"p0567","text":"(b) RevMed will not, and will cause its Affiliates and (sub)contractors not to, use any government or not-for-profit organization funding that would encumber the RevMed Licensed Technology without the prior written consent of Sanofi, which consent may be withheld in Sanofi's sole discretion. For clarity, this Section 13.3(b) does not apply to Permitted Contractors and Researchers."},{"id":"p0568","text":"(c) At any time upon written request from Sanofi, if the Parties mutually agree that an agreement between RevMed and a Permitted Contractor or Researcher should be amended to optimize language regarding assignment of inventions or intellectual property to ensure conformance with the principles relating thereto set forth in this Agreement, RevMed will use Commercially Reasonable Efforts to cause such Permitted Contractors or Researchers to sign written agreements substantially in the form agreed upon by the Parties. 69"},{"id":"p0569","text":"(d) With respect to the sponsored research agreements of RevMed in effect as of the Effective Date, if after the Effective Date, there is a material amendment or modification to any such sponsored research agreement or work plan thereunder, and if Sanofi in good faith desires to assume and perform the subject research in-house and if Sanofi reasonably possesses the relevant expertise, capacity and applicable materials necessary for such research at such time (the \"Capabilities\"), then Sanofi shall notify RevMed and if RevMed does not give notice to terminate such sponsored research agreement to the applicable Third Party under such agreement within [***] after Sanofi reasonably demonstrates that it has the Capabilities for such research activities, then RevMed shall obtain a license to the intellectual property rights in any inventions arising out of such sponsored research such that they are \"Controlled\" by RevMed for purposes of this Agreement and RevMed shall [***]."},{"id":"p0570","text":"13.4 Mutual Covenants."},{"id":"p0571","text":"(a) No Debarment. In the course of the Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of the Products, neither Party nor its Affiliates shall use any employee or consultant who has been debarred by any Regulatory Authority or, to such Party's or its Affiliates' Knowledge, is the subject of debarment proceedings by a Regulatory Authority. Each Party shall notify the other Party promptly upon becoming aware (in the case of Sanofi, by its compliance department) that any of its or its Affiliates' employees or consultants has been debarred or is the subject of debarment proceedings by any Regulatory Authority."},{"id":"p0572","text":"(b) Compliance. Each Party and its Affiliates shall comply in all material respects with all Applicable Law (including all anti-bribery laws and laws applicable to the manufacture of human pharmaceuticals) in the Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of the Products and performance of its obligations under this Agreement and the Ancillary Agreements."},{"id":"p0573","text":"(c) Information. In addition to the requirements of Section 6.5, each Party will provide the other Party with all information in its control reasonably necessary or desirable for such other Party to comply with its pharmacovigilance responsibilities in all countries in the Territory, including, as applicable, any adverse drug experiences (including those events or experiences that are required to be reported to the FDA under 21 C.F.R. §§ 312.32 or 314.80 or to foreign Regulatory Authorities under corresponding Applicable Law outside the United States of America) from pre-clinical or clinical laboratory, animal toxicology, pharmacology studies and clinical studies, in each case in the form reasonably requested by such other Party."},{"id":"p0574","text":"13.5 No Other Warranties. EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS ARTICLE XIII, (A) NO REPRESENTATION, CONDITION OR WARRANTY WHATSOEVER IS MADE OR GIVEN BY OR ON BEHALF OF SANOFI OR REVMED; AND (B) ALL OTHER CONDITIONS AND WARRANTIES WHETHER WRITTEN OR ORAL OR EXPRESS OR IMPLIED ARE HEREBY EXPRESSLY EXCLUDED, INCLUDING ANY CONDITIONS AND WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE OR NON-INFRINGEMENT. 70"},{"id":"p0575","text":"13.6 Closing Conditions. The obligations of each Party to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and the Ancillary Agreements (the \"Contemplated Transactions\") is subject to the fulfillment, or, to the extent permitted by Applicable Law, waiver by such Party, of each of the following conditions (collectively, the \"Closing Conditions\"):"},{"id":"p0576","text":"(a) The representations and warranties of the other Party contained in this Agreement (i) that are not qualified by materiality, material adverse effect, substantial compliance or similar materiality qualifier will be true and correct in all material respects both when made and at the closing with the same force and effect as if made on the Effective Date and (ii) that are qualified by materiality, material adverse effect, substantial compliance or similar materiality qualifier will be true and correct in all respects both when made and at the closing with the same force and effect as if made on the Effective Date, except, in each of (i) and (ii) as would not reasonably be expected, individually or in the aggregate, to have a material impact on the transaction contemplated by this Agreement."},{"id":"p0577","text":"(b) All actions by (including any authorization, consent or approval) in respect of (including notice to), or filings with, any Governmental Authority or other Person that are required to be obtained pursuant to Section 3.8 to consummate the Contemplated Transactions (including any HSR/Antitrust Filing) will have been obtained or made, in a manner reasonably satisfactory in form and substance to such Party, and no such authorization, consent or approval will have been revoked."},{"id":"p0578","text":"(c) No Material Adverse Event shall have occurred or arisen since the Execution Date."},{"id":"p0579","text":"Article XIV."}]}

{"sectionRef":"§ RESEARCH","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0282","text":"RESEARCH"},{"id":"p0283","text":"4.1 General. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Parties will conduct a research program for the identification, validation and optimization of SHP2 Inhibitors (including without limitation back-up compound chemistry and characterization, pre-clinical studies, and translation and biomarker studies) pursuant to a research plan (such plan, the \"Research Plan\")."},{"id":"p0284","text":"4.2 Research Plan."},{"id":"p0285","text":"(a) Research Plan and Budget."},{"id":"p0286","text":"(i) Initial. As of the Effective Date, the Parties have agreed on an initial Research Plan and Research Budget for Calendar Years 2018, 2019 and 2020, which is set forth in Exhibit H of the Correspondence."},{"id":"p0287","text":"A. Calendar Year 2018. The initial Research Plan and Research Budget for Calendar Year 2018 are final and may only be amended or modified by mutual agreement of the Parties (i.e., Sanofi shall not have the unilateral right, either directly or through its participation in the JRDC or the JSC, including by exercising its final decision-making power under Section 2.10(b), [***])."},{"id":"p0288","text":"B. Calendar Years 2019 and 2020. The initial Research Budget for Calendar Years 2019 and 2020 included in Exhibit H of the Correspondence represents, as of the Effective Date, what the Parties believe to be a reasonable estimate of the Research Budget for Calendar Years 2019 and 2020 and shall become final only if the Parties mutually agree in writing with respect to the detailed Research activities and timelines to be set forth in the Research Plan for Calendar Years 2019 and 2020. Upon any such mutual agreement, such Research Plan and Research Budget may only be amended or modified by mutual agreement of the Parties (i.e., Sanofi shall not have the right to exercise its final decision-making power under Section 2.10(b), [***]. If the Parties do not reach such mutual agreement and Sanofi exercises its final decision-making power under Section 2.10(b) [***]. For clarity, if the Parties mutually agree upon activities under the Research Plan for a Research Budget equal to or greater than that set forth in Exhibit H of the Correspondence then Section 4.5(b) shall apply and Sanofi shall be responsible for 80% of the Research and Development Costs and RevMed shall be responsible for 20% of the Research and Development Costs, provided that Sanofi shall be responsible for [***]% of the Research and Development Costs associated with [***]. 31"},{"id":"p0289","text":"C. Calendar Year 2021 and Beyond. The Research Plan and Research Budget for Calendar Year 2021 and any Calendar Year after 2021 shall be subject in all respects to the governance set forth in Article II (including Sanofi's final decision-making power under Section 2.10(b) and the procedure for amendments set forth in Section 4.2(a)(ii))."},{"id":"p0290","text":"(ii) Amendments. From time to time after the Effective Date, the JRDC may propose any amendment to the Research Plan, which shall be made in good faith, based on scientific and regulatory judgment. The Research Plan shall set forth: (a) the Research activities to be conducted by either Party; (b) the estimated timelines for such Research activities; and (c) a detailed budget setting forth the estimated RevMed R&D Costs to be incurred in connection with such activities (the \"Research Budget\"). If the terms of the Research Plan contradict, or create inconsistencies or ambiguities with, the terms of this Agreement, then the terms of this Agreement shall govern."},{"id":"p0291","text":"(b) Conduct of Research. Each Party shall perform all Research activities under this Agreement in compliance with all Applicable Law (including GMP, GLP and GCP). In furtherance and not in limitation of the foregoing, RevMed shall use diligent efforts to conduct its activities under each Research Plan in accordance with the terms of such Research Plan (including timelines), as the same may be amended from time to time (and which basis for comparison shall be tolled until any then-contemplated or pending amendments are completed or for the duration of any bona fide dispute between the Parties with respect to a Research Plan or amendment thereto), and this Agreement. If Sanofi believes RevMed has materially breached its obligation in the foregoing sentences with respect to any Product, Sanofi shall so notify RevMed in writing."},{"id":"p0292","text":"If either RevMed agrees or it is determined in accordance with [***], that RevMed has committed a material breach of its obligations under this Section 4.2(b) with respect to such Product, the JRDC shall, within [***] after such agreement on or determination of material breach, meet in person or by teleconference to discuss such material breach and specify reasonable actions that RevMed should take to cure such material breach. If RevMed fails to commence within [***] after such discussion occurs such actions recommended by the JRDC, or fails to cure any such material breach within [***] after the JRDC meets (or such longer timeframe as the JRDC decides is necessary to complete the actions specified by the JRDC), then Sanofi shall have the right, without prejudice to any other rights or remedies Sanofi may have under this Agreement or otherwise at law or in equity, [***]."},{"id":"p0293","text":"In such case, RevMed shall, [***], (i) make available [***], (ii) provide [***], and (iii) otherwise provide [***]."},{"id":"p0294","text":"4.3 Designation of Development Candidates As of the Effective Date, the Parties agree that the SHP2 Inhibitor set forth on Exhibit I of the Correspondence is deemed a Development Candidate (defined below) under this Agreement. From time to time, either Party may nominate one or more additional SHP2 Inhibitors to the JRDC for consideration as a candidate for Development under a Development Plan (the \"Development Candidate\"). Such nomination (and approval thereof by the JRDC) shall be made prior to the initiation of the IND-enabling studies for such SHP2 Inhibitor(s), unless otherwise permitted by the JRDC. Promptly after such nomination, each Party shall present to the JRDC the data and results it has obtained with respect to such SHP2 Inhibitor(s) as well as, if requested by the other Party, written records maintained 32"},{"id":"p0295","text":"by or on behalf of such Party or its Affiliates with respect to the discovery or development history of such SHP2 Inhibitor. The JRDC shall determine whether such SHP2 Inhibitor(s) shall be approved as a Development Candidate under this Agreement. The JRDC may also request that further Research activities be conducted with respect to such SHP2 Inhibitor(s) (under an amended Research Plan), after which activities such SHP2 Inhibitor(s) may be reconsidered for nomination as a Development Candidate. If the JRDC (or Designated Senior Officers, as applicable) approve a particular SHP2 Inhibitor as a Development Candidate, then the Parties shall proceed to conduct further Development of such SHP2 Inhibitor (including IND-enabling studies, other pre-clinical and non-clinical studies, and clinical studies) pursuant to a Development Plan (as further described in Section 5.2) and under the oversight of the JRDC. In addition, at any time after a SHP2 Inhibitor is designated as a Development Candidate, if requested by Sanofi, RevMed shall make available written records (such as lab notebooks) maintained by or on behalf of RevMed or its Affiliates with respect to the discovery and/or development history of such SHP2 Inhibitor or any Product under Development that contains such SHP2 Inhibitor, provided that such request shall not be made more than once for each SHP2 Inhibitor or each Product, as applicable, except for cause."},{"id":"p0296","text":"4.4 Research Records and Reports. Each Party shall maintain complete, current and accurate records of all Research activities conducted by it hereunder, and all data and other information resulting from such activities. Such records shall fully and properly reflect all work done and results achieved in the performance of the Research activities in good scientific manner appropriate for regulatory and patent purposes. Each Party shall keep the other Party reasonably informed as to its progress in the conduct of the Research activities through meetings of the JRDC. Upon written request from the JRDC, each Party shall submit to the JRDC a written summary (in slide format unless otherwise agreed by the Parties) of its Research activities since its prior report."},{"id":"p0297","text":"4.5 Research Costs."},{"id":"p0298","text":"(a) Calendar Years 2018, 2021 and All Calendar Years After 2021. Sanofi shall be responsible for 100% of the Research and Development Costs for Calendar Years 2018, 2021 and all Calendar Years after 2021. Sanofi will reimburse RevMed for any RevMed R&D Costs incurred by or on behalf of RevMed after the Execution Date in the performance of its activities under the Research Plan, provided that such RevMed R&D Costs are incurred per the Research Budget for such activities as approved by the JSC and [***] set forth in the Research Budget for the particular Calendar Quarter. Promptly following the end of each Calendar Quarter during which RevMed is responsible for activities under the Research Plan, but in no event later than [***] following the end of such Calendar Quarter, RevMed will provide to Sanofi a detailed expense report in form approved by the JRDC with respect to the RevMed R&D Costs incurred by or on behalf of RevMed during such Calendar Quarter consistent with the previous sentence (including, if requested by Sanofi in writing, copies of receipts or invoices from Third Parties for all RevMed R&D Out-of-Pocket Costs) together with an invoice for the same, provided that[***]. Sanofi will reimburse RevMed in Dollars all undisputed amounts within such expense reports under this Section 4.5 within [***] following receipt of the invoice therefor. RevMed shall invoice Sanofi for costs under this Section 4.5 on an accrual basis. 33"},{"id":"p0299","text":"(b) Calendar Years 2019 and 2020. Subject to Section 4.2(a)(i)(B), Sanofi shall be responsible for 80% of the Research and Development Costs for Calendar Years 2019 and 2020 and RevMed shall be responsible for 20% of the Research and Development Costs for Calendar Years 2019 and 2020 (provided that such Research and Development Costs are incurred per the Research Budget for such activities as approved by the JSC and [***] set forth in the Research Budget for the particular Calendar Quarter). Research and Development Costs shall initially be borne by the Party incurring the cost or expense."},{"id":"p0300","text":"Promptly following the end of each Calendar Quarter during Calendar Years 2019 and 2020, but in no event later than [***] following the end of such Calendar Quarter, each Party will provide to the JRDC a detailed expense report in form approved by the JRDC with respect to the Research and Development Costs incurred by or on behalf of such Party during such Calendar Quarter consistent with the previous sentence (including, if requested by Sanofi in writing, copies of receipts or invoices from Third Parties for all RevMed R&D Out-of-Pocket Costs). The Party that incurs more than its share of the total Research and Development Costs during any such Calendar Quarter shall deliver an invoice to the other Party for an amount of cash sufficient to reconcile to the invoicing Party's agreed percentage of Research and Development Costs."},{"id":"p0301","text":"Such other Party will reimburse the invoicing Party in Dollars all undisputed amounts within such expense reports under this Section 4.5 in accordance with Section 9.5 mutatis mutandis."},{"id":"p0302","text":"Article V."}]}

input.quote: 14.6 Insurance. Each Party shall procure and maintain insurance, including product liability insurance, with respect to its activities hereunder and under the Ancillary Agreements and which is consistent with normal business practices of companies similarly situated at all times during which any SHP2 Inhibitors or Product is being clinically tested in human subjects or commercially distributed or sold. Sanofi may fulfill such obligation through self- insurance.
input.rationale: An insurance clause is present at § 14.6, so the rule is satisfied rather than missing. It obliges each Party (including RevMed) to carry insurance appropriate to its activities, expressly including product liability cover — the risk that matters in this clinical development/commercialization collaboration, as opposed to a hosting or data-processing engagement. It also gives us certificates/evidence on request and, one-way in our favour, requires RevMed to notify Sanofi ahead of cancellation, non-renewal or material change. Two further provisions run in our favour and should not be disturbed: Sanofi may satisfy the requirement through self-insurance, and insurance is expressly not a cap on either Party's Article XIV indemnification obligations. The clause sets limits by reference to "normal business practices of companies similarly situated" rather than the preferred stated figures (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M); we note that as a sub-element short of preferred wording, not a material failure, given this is a bilateral pharma collaboration in which RevMed does not process Customer Data or work on our premises, so the cyber/E&O-driven fallback limits are not the operative exposure. Effectively at the fallback: a substantive, mutual insurance covenant with evidence and cancellation-notice mechanics, but without express dollar limits. No redline proposed.

input.rationale: Section 15.2 meets the preferred position. We may assign to any Sanofi Affiliate without RevMed's consent (p0610) and, without consent, to a successor in a merger, acquisition or similar transaction or a sale of all or substantially all related assets (p0611), giving us the affiliate and M&A carve-out we require. RevMed must obtain our consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned) for affiliate assignments and cannot transfer the RevMed Licensed Patents to a Third Party without our consent (p0615). RevMed's reciprocal right to assign to a Change of Control successor without consent sits at the fallback level and is mitigated by the Acquiror Family firewall conditions in p0613-p0614 (acquired party remains a wholly-owned subsidiary, IP and R&D assets stay with the Acquired Party Family, separation from Acquiror competing programs, no Know-How exchange) and by our own option to terminate on a RevMed Change of Control under Section 12.2(a)(ii) (p0489). Critically, no RevMed termination or re-pricing right is triggered by a Sanofi change of control; RevMed's termination rights run only to material breach, insolvency, competing product and cessation. Noted but not flagged: the Section 9.7(a) tax gross-up where withholding arises from a Sanofi assignment to an Affiliate, and the cessation of post-termination royalties payable to us on a Change of Control of Sanofi (p0508), are narrow economic consequences rather than vendor exit or re-pricing rights.

Parties: we represent Aventis, Inc. (Sanofi); counterparty is Revolution Medicines, Inc. (RevMed).

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

<parameter name="rationale">Section 15.2 meets (and in places exceeds) our preferred position. We may assign to any Sanofi Affiliate without RevMed's consent (p0610) and, without consent, to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition or similar transaction or a sale of all or substantially all related assets (p0611) — the M&A/affiliate carve-out we require. RevMed, by contrast, needs our consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned) for affiliate assignments, may not transfer the RevMed Licensed Patents to a Third Party without our consent (p0615), and its permitted Change of Control assignment is conditioned on firewall protections (wholly-owned subsidiary, IP and R&D assets retained, separation from Acquiror Family competing programs, no Know-How exchange) (p0613–p0614), which functions as the competitor protection our playbook seeks. RevMed's mutual right to assign to a Change of Control successor without consent sits at the fallback ("mutual right to assign to successors"), and is offset by our own termination/alternative option on a RevMed Change of Control (Section 12.2(a)(ii), p0489). Critically, no RevMed termination or re-pricing right is triggered by a Sanofi change of control — RevMed's termination rights run only to material breach, insolvency, competing product and cessation. Two minor points noted but not flagged: (i) Section 9.7(a) requires us to gross up withholding tax arising from an assignment to an Affiliate, and (ii) post-termination royalties payable to us under Section 12.3 cease on a Sanofi Change of Control (p0508) — each a narrow economic consequence rather than a vendor exit or re-pricing right on our change of control.</rationale>

**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

§ 14.6 of the agreement contains a usable insurance covenant, so this rule is not "missing." Key points:

- **Mutual obligation** — each Party must procure and maintain insurance for its activities, expressly including **product liability** cover, which is the operative exposure in a clinical development and commercialization collaboration rather than the cyber/E&O exposure the playbook's preferred limits are calibrated to.
- **Runs in our favour in two respects** — Sanofi may satisfy the requirement through **self-insurance**, and RevMed (one-way) must give advance written notice of cancellation, non-renewal or material change. We also get evidence of insurance on request.
- **No cap effect** — insurance is expressly not construed as a limit on either Party's Article XIV indemnification obligations.

Noted but not flagged: limits are set by reference to "normal business practices of companies similarly situated" rather than the preferred stated figures (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M). That is a sub-element short of the preferred wording, not a material failure — RevMed is not a hosting/data-processing vendor here and does not work on our premises, so the clause sits at the fallback and is acceptable as drafted.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

- **Competitor protection:** RevMed's consent-free Change of Control assignment is conditioned on the Acquiror Family firewall in p0613–p0614 (wholly-owned subsidiary, IP/R&D assets retained, separation from Acquiror competing programs, no Know-How exchange). RevMed's reciprocal successor right sits at the fallback ("mutual right to assign to successors") and is offset by our termination/alternative option on a RevMed Change of Control (Section 12.2(a)(ii), p0489).
- **No walk-away trigger:** RevMed has no termination or re-pricing right on a Sanofi change of control; its termination rights run only to material breach, insolvency, competing product and cessation.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged as deviations: the Section 9.7(a) withholding gross-up where tax arises from our assignment to an Affiliate, and the cessation of post-termination royalties payable to us upon a Change of Control of Sanofi (p0508) — narrow economic points, not vendor exit rights.

**Finding: Compliant** (MINCOMMIT — no redline)

The Agreement contains no take-or-pay exposure for Sanofi:

- **No commitment mechanics exist.** Searches for "minimum", "shortfall", and purchase-commitment phrasing return no applicable provisions anywhere in the document.
- **Forecasts are expressly non-binding.** The only volume-related mechanics are Commercialization Plan inputs at §8.2 — "non-binding sales and marketing forecasts" and "non-binding net sales projections" (p0370, p0371, p0373).
- **Supply is unquantified.** §7.3 (p0360) only requires the Parties to "negotiate in good faith to enter into a supply agreement... on commercially reasonable terms," with no committed volumes or shortfall payment.
- **Sanofi retains control.** §8.1 and §8.3 give Sanofi sole right over order processing, invoicing, pricing and distribution (p0363, p0375), so there are no volume caps on our side either.

This sits at the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback. Diligence/Commercially Reasonable Efforts obligations are a separate commercial term handled under another rule and were not double-flagged here.

Parties: we represent Aventis, Inc. (Sanofi); counterparty is Revolution Medicines, Inc. (RevMed).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: Each Party shall perform all Research activities under this Agreement in compliance with all Applicable Law (including GMP, GLP and GCP). In furtherance and not in limitation of the foregoing, RevMed shall use diligent efforts to conduct its activities under each Research Plan in accordance with the terms of such Research Plan (including timelines)
input.rationale: This is an R&D collaboration and license, not a software/services procurement, so the rule maps onto the performance-standard and warranty package rather than a conformance-to-documentation period. RevMed is bound to a real performance standard (Section 4.2(b): all Research activities in compliance with Applicable Law including GMP, GLP and GCP, plus diligent efforts to follow the Research Plan and timelines), gives a compliance-with-laws warranty on all prior research (13.2(u)) and a continuing mutual compliance covenant (13.4(b)), and gives an extensive suite of title, non-infringement and IP-integrity warranties in 13.2. The remedy path is meaningful and better than repair/replace/refund: a JRDC-supervised cure process with specified corrective actions and step-in/other rights for Sanofi if RevMed fails to cure (p0292), express indemnification for material breach of RevMed's warranties (p0583), and termination for material breach. The 13.5 disclaimer expressly preserves everything stated in Article XIII, which is where all express warranties sit, so it does not swallow the express warranty and this is nowhere near "AS IS" walk-away territory. Two sub-elements short of the preferred wording are noted but not flagged: RevMed's 13.2 warranties are made as of the Execution Date only (mitigated by the closing bring-down in 13.6(a)), and the 13.5 carve-out is drafted by reference to "THIS ARTICLE XIII" rather than the whole Agreement, so warranty-like commitments elsewhere (e.g., Section 4.2(b)) rely on their status as covenants rather than warranties.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Aventis, Inc. (Sanofi); counterparty is Revolution Medicines, Inc. (RevMed).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: Each Party shall perform all Research activities under this Agreement in compliance with all Applicable Law (including GMP, GLP and GCP). In furtherance and not in limitation of the foregoing, RevMed shall use diligent efforts to conduct its activities under each Research Plan in accordance with the terms of such Research Plan (including timelines)
input.rationale: This is an R&D collaboration and license, not a software/services procurement, so the rule maps onto the performance-standard and warranty package rather than a conformance-to-documentation period. RevMed is bound to a real performance standard (Section 4.2(b): all Research activities in compliance with Applicable Law including GMP, GLP and GCP, plus diligent efforts to follow the Research Plan and timelines), gives a compliance-with-laws warranty on all prior research (13.2(u)) and a continuing mutual compliance covenant (13.4(b)), and gives an extensive suite of title, non-infringement and IP-integrity warranties in 13.2. The remedy path is meaningful and better than repair/replace/refund: a JRDC-supervised cure process with specified corrective actions and step-in/other rights for Sanofi if RevMed fails to cure (p0292), express indemnification for material breach of RevMed's warranties (p0583), and termination for material breach. The 13.5 disclaimer expressly preserves everything stated in Article XIII, which is where all express warranties sit, so it does not swallow the express warranty and this is nowhere near "AS IS" walk-away territory. **Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The WARRANTY rule maps onto this collaboration/license rather than a software or services purchase, so I assessed the performance standard, the warranty package and the remedy path:

- **Performance standard** — §4.2(b) (p0291) binds RevMed to conduct all Research activities in compliance with Applicable Law including GMP, GLP and GCP, and to use diligent efforts to follow the Research Plan and its timelines. That is the functional equivalent of the "professional and workmanlike" standard.
- **Compliance with laws** — §13.2(u) (past research in material compliance) plus the continuing mutual covenant in §13.4(b), backed by FCPA and debarment reps in §13.1.
- **Remedy** — stronger than repair/replace/refund: a JRDC cure process with specified corrective actions and step-in/other rights for Sanofi on failure to cure (p0292), indemnification for material breach of RevMed's warranties (p0583), and termination for material breach.
- **Disclaimer** — §13.5 expressly preserves everything stated in Article XIII, where all express warranties live, so it does not swallow the express warranty; this is not an "AS IS" position.

Noted in the rationale but deliberately not flagged as deviations: RevMed's §13.2 warranties are Execution-Date-only (mitigated by the §13.6(a) closing bring-down), and the §13.5 carve-out references "THIS ARTICLE XIII" rather than the whole Agreement, so §4.2(b) relies on its character as a covenant. Neither is material enough to fail the fallback, and the conformance-to-documentation / no-malicious-code elements have no application absent software or deliverables.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

Use the document tools for any needed source inspection. Call propose_redline until it returns ok:true, then submit exactly once with the locked status and stop.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule prose and mirrored atomic drafting checklist:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

"Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains a full exit/transition architecture, so no insert is needed. Section 11.6 (surviving under Section 12.4) is a mutual return/destruction-and-written-certification mechanic triggered on termination only on a party's written request, with express carve-outs allowing retention of information needed for continuing rights and obligations plus archival copies — so there is no "immediate deletion / no data return" walk-away risk against us, and on expiry our licences become perpetual and fully paid up (12.3(b)). Section 12.3(c)(vi) plus 12.3(c)(iv) set out detailed transition assistance, know-how and regulatory/clinical data transfer with defined time and effort limits, and Section 12.3(e) requires RevMed to provide copies of materials and "all reasonable assistance" to us on a change-of-control termination. These transition duties run principally from Sanofi to RevMed, which is the ordinary bargain in a licence-back on termination and is not an issue to flag on our side; the effort/duration caps and the [***] time periods in 12.3(c)(vi) are the terms to confirm commercially rather than a playbook breach. Direction and structure aside, the clause set meets the fallback (data/know-how transfer within defined post-termination windows and time-limited transition assistance), and the redacted durations are the only open point, noted rather than redlined.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Aventis, Inc. (Sanofi); counterparty is Revolution Medicines, Inc. (RevMed).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains a full exit/transition architecture, so no insert is needed. Section 11.6 (surviving under Section 12.4) is a mutual return/destruction-and-written-certification mechanic triggered on termination only on a party's written request, with express carve-outs allowing retention of information needed for continuing rights and obligations plus archival copies — so there is no "immediate deletion / no data return" walk-away risk against us, and on expiry our licences become perpetual and fully paid up (12.3(b)). Section 12.3(c)(vi) plus 12.3(c)(iv) set out detailed transition assistance, know-how and regulatory/clinical data transfer with defined time and effort limits, and Section 12.3(e) requires RevMed to provide copies of materials and "all reasonable assistance" to us on a change-of-control termination. These transition duties run principally from Sanofi to RevMed, which is the ordinary bargain in a licence-back on termination and is not an issue to flag on our side; the effort/duration caps and the [***] time periods in 12.3(c)(vi) are the terms to confirm commercially rather than a playbook breach. Direction and structure aside, the clause set meets the fallback (data/know-how transfer within defined post-termination windows and time-limited transition assistance), and the redacted durations are the only open point, noted rather than redlined.

**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The TRANSITION rule is satisfied in substance, and the vendor-side framing of the rule does not map cleanly onto this collaboration:

- **Data return / deletion:** Section 11.6 (p0477) is a mutual, request-triggered return/destruction provision with written confirmation of destruction, and it expressly survives termination via Section 12.4 (p0532). Retention carve-outs for continuing rights/obligations and archival copies mean there is no "immediate deletion / no return" walk-away exposure for us. On expiry, our licences go perpetual, royalty-free and fully paid up (p0499).
- **Transition assistance:** Section 12.3(c)(vi) (p0516–p0525) plus 12.3(c)(iv) (p0512–p0514) provide a detailed, time-bounded transition regime (regulatory materials, pharmacovigilance data, know-how transfer, manufacturing tech transfer, clinical trial transfer, orderly-transition cooperation), and Section 12.3(e) (p0531) requires RevMed to provide copies and "all reasonable assistance" to us on a change-of-control termination.
- **Direction:** the bulk of these obligations run from Sanofi to RevMed, which is the standard licence-back bargain on termination — not something to flag against ourselves.

Noted (not flagged): the durations and effort caps in 12.3(c)(iv) and (vi) are redacted, so the practical length of our assistance obligations and the assistance available to us should be confirmed commercially rather than redlined here.

Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

Use the document tools for any needed source inspection. Call propose_redline until it returns ok:true, then submit exactly once with the locked status and stop.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule prose and mirrored atomic drafting checklist:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):

]

- Clause as redlined sits at the fallback (mutual 12-month cap with indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct carve-outs).
