system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

Use the document tools for any needed source inspection. Call propose_redline until it returns ok:true, then submit exactly once with the locked status and stop.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule prose and mirrored atomic drafting checklist:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-26ebcb22","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"INDEMNIFICATION; LIABILITY; INSURANCE","rationale":"A counterparty indemnity in our favour is present and materially satisfies the rule. Section 14.1 requires RevMed to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Sanofi and its Affiliates (and their officers, directors, agents and employees) against Third Party Claims and Losses arising from (a) RevMed's negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct, (b) material breach of its representations and warranties, and (c) material breach of its obligations. Because RevMed's Article XIII warranties include IP ownership/right to license, non-infringement of Third Party patents and non-misappropriation of Third Party Know-How (p0545-p0552) and compliance with Applicable Law (p0542, p0564), third-party IP claims and breach-of-law claims are captured through limb (b)/(c). Section 14.3 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice with no forfeiture for late notice, indemnitor's option to control defence, right to participate, settlement consent for non-monetary relief, cooperation with cost reimbursement), and Section 14.5 expressly carves indemnification under Sections 14.1/14.2 out of the liability limitation, so RevMed's indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback's 3x-fees super-cap. Insurance backstops it (p0603). Two sub-elements fall short of the ideal preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: there is no standalone allegation-based IP infringement indemnity with procure/modify/replace/refund remedies (instead Section 10.7 allocates third-party licence-taking, with Sanofi holding the first right), and the patent non-infringement warranty is knowledge-qualified. Sanofi's reciprocal indemnity in Section 14.2 is broader than \"Customer content plus breach of law\" in that it covers Sanofi's own Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of Products, but that follows inevitably from our role as the exploiting licensee in a collaboration/licence structure (not a vendor services deal) and is subject to full carve-outs for RevMed's negligence, warranty breach and breach of obligations, so it is not a one-way indemnity or walk-away outcome. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-1f23ff51","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS","rationale":"Article X allocates ownership of Program Inventions on an inventorship basis (Sanofi Sole Program Know-How/Patents remain Sanofi's under §§1.109/10.1(a)), so there is no assignment of Sanofi IP, data or funded results to RevMed. Joint Program Technology is jointly owned, but §10.1(b) gives each Party an unrestricted right to exploit and license it without duty of accounting or consent, plus a perpetual, irrevocable, fully-paid worldwide licence with sublicensing rights where needed outside the US — so the joint ownership is not the \"joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit\" walk-away, and RevMed's own interest is further subordinated to Sanofi's exclusive licences and payment obligations (in our favour). Sanofi also takes an exclusive licence under all RevMed Licensed Technology (§3.1), receives assignment of all Regulatory Approvals/INDs/NDAs once RevMed completes its Clinical Trials (§6.2), and each Party must flow down invention-assignment (or, failing that, a perpetual, fully-paid, exclusive, royalty-free licence) obligations to Third Parties and subcontractors (§10.1(a), §3.5). Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording are noted only: §10.1(a) is materially redacted ([***]) so the precise inventorship allocation cannot be fully verified, and there is no separate \"Customer Data\" ownership sentence (data is handled through the Program Inventions/Know-How and regulatory ownership constructs appropriate to a collaboration). No redline warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-91954257","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Section 15.2 meets the preferred position. We may assign to any Sanofi Affiliate without RevMed's consent (p0610) and, without consent, to a successor in a merger, acquisition or similar transaction or a sale of all or substantially all related assets (p0611), giving us the affiliate and M&A carve-out we require. RevMed must obtain our consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned) for affiliate assignments and cannot transfer the RevMed Licensed Patents to a Third Party without our consent (p0615). RevMed's reciprocal right to assign to a Change of Control successor without consent sits at the fallback level and is mitigated by the Acquiror Family firewall conditions in p0613-p0614 (acquired party remains a wholly-owned subsidiary, IP and R&D assets stay with the Acquired Party Family, separation from Acquiror competing programs, no Know-How exchange) and by our own option to terminate on a RevMed Change of Control under Section 12.2(a)(ii) (p0489). Critically, no RevMed termination or re-pricing right is triggered by a Sanofi change of control; RevMed's termination rights run only to material breach, insolvency, competing product and cessation. Noted but not flagged: the Section 9.7(a) tax gross-up where withholding arises from a Sanofi assignment to an Affiliate, and the cessation of post-termination royalties payable to us on a Change of Control of Sanofi (p0508), are narrow economic consequences rather than vendor exit or re-pricing rights.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-8e0876d1","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"LICENSE","rationale":"The Agreement contains no exclusivity, \"sole supplier\" or requirements obligation binding us. All exclusivity runs in our favour: the Article III licences are exclusive to Sanofi even as to RevMed (p0248, p0250), and Section 3.6 and Section 10.x confirm exclusivity operates for the licensee's benefit (p0265, p0424). Manufacturing/supply (Sections 7.1–7.3) imposes no obligation to source Product solely from RevMed — supply is to be agreed under a future Supply Agreement and RevMed must even help us establish our own third-party supply (p0359). This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity on Customer), so no redline. Two inbound constraints noted but not deviations: (i) RevMed's one-time exclusive Co-Promotion Option over a share of U.S. Detailing (p0380) is a negotiated co-promotion right conditioned on RevMed demonstrating resources to our reasonable satisfaction and lapsing if not timely exercised, not an exclusive-dealing covenant; and (ii) Section 12.2(d) gives RevMed a termination right if we pursue a Competing Product in narrow circumstances (p0493), which does not prohibit us from developing or buying elsewhere and includes an election to avoid termination.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-a10c97b9","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum/early-termination fee payable by us. Searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalty\", \"termination fee\" and \"minimum\" return nothing, and Sanofi's termination for convenience right (Section 12.2(a)(i)) is exercisable on notice alone — the effects of termination in Section 12.3(c) are limited to reversion of licenses, transition assistance and inventory transfer (with RevMed paying for inventory and post-termination royalties to us), not a compensatory payment by us. This meets the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages. Two adjacent items are noted but not deviations under this rule: Section 9.6 late-payment interest is mutual (payable by whichever Party pays late) and capped at the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, which is ordinary default interest rather than a penalty; and Section 15.6(f) bars the arbitrators from awarding punitive or exemplary damages, which operates in our favour. The upfront, milestone and royalty amounts in Article IX are negotiated consideration, not liquidated damages.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-120b9b18","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"LICENSE","rationale":"The grant to us in Section 3.1(a) (p0248) is an exclusive, royalty-bearing licence under the RevMed Licensed Technology across Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialisation in the Field and Licensed Territory, and it is not revocable at RevMed's discretion: RevMed may terminate only for uncured material breach, insolvency, or the defined Competing Product / cessation triggers, each with notice and cure (p0491, p0493, p0495). Scope reaches our affiliates and contractors as the preferred position requires — Section 3.4(a) lets us act through any Affiliate without RevMed's consent, 3.4(b) permits multi-tier sublicensing to Third Parties, and 3.4(c) permits subcontracting as we deem appropriate. Successor transfer is expressly permitted without consent in an M&A/asset sale (p0611), and on expiration the licence becomes \"fully paid up, royalty free, perpetual and irrevocable\" (p0499). Two minor sub-elements fall short of the ideal but are not material deviations and are noted rather than redlined: sublicensing substantially all US rights requires RevMed's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) under 3.4(b)(ii), and the RevMed termination triggers in 12.2(d)-(e) go slightly beyond pure material breach.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-251aa9c4","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"The Agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use covenant binding Sanofi, which meets the preferred position. Searches for \"compete\", \"shall not develop\", \"Sanofi shall not / will not\" and \"Exclusivity\" return no restrictive covenant on Sanofi; the only covenants running against Sanofi are the mutual debarment/compliance/pharmacovigilance covenants in Section 13.4, and Section 13.3 covenants bind RevMed only. The licensed \"Field\" is defined as \"any and all uses\" (p0053), so there is no field limitation on our business, and Section 3.8 expressly provides that neither Party must \"agree to any restrictions on the businesses of RevMed or Sanofi or its Affiliates\" to obtain clearance (p0271). The functional restraint the planner flagged, Section 12.2(d), is not a prohibition: Sanofi remains free to develop, manufacture or commercialize a Competing Product, and the sole consequence is a RevMed termination right that (i) arises only after a stated period, (ii) is unavailable once Sanofi has commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product, (iii) operates during the Term only with no post-term restraint, and (iv) can be defeated by a Sanofi written election. The resulting reversion/transition consequences in Section 12.3(c) are the same package that applies to Sanofi's own termination for convenience, so they are not an incremental competitive restraint. The Section 15.2 Acquiror-Family separation conditions in (A)-(D) attach to the RevMed-as-acquired-Party case (p0613/p0614); for Sanofi, p0612 excludes acquirer IP and the Acquiror Family unconditionally, which favours us. Two sub-elements fall short of an ideal draft and are noted rather than flagged: the \"Competing Product\" definition (p0037) is redacted, so its breadth cannot be fully verified, and there is no express carve-out for internal development or acquisitions in Section 12.2(d) — but as 12.2(d) creates only a termination right rather than a covenant, this does not restrict our business and no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-44409091","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"Section 12.2(a)(i) gives us (Sanofi) an express, unilateral termination-for-convenience right on written notice, exercisable in the entirety or on a country-by-country / Product-by-Product basis, which is the preferred position (customer convenience exit, partial termination included). RevMed has no corresponding convenience right: its termination rights are all for cause — material breach (12.2(b)), insolvency (12.2(c)), Sanofi's development of a Competing Product (12.2(d)) and Sanofi's cessation of development (12.2(e)) — so there is no vendor mid-term walk-away. No early-termination fee or penalty is imposed on us for a convenience termination; the exit consequences in 12.3(c) are a grant-back/transition package customary for a license and collaboration of this type, and RevMed in fact pays us post-termination royalties on Termination Products (12.3(c)(ii)C), which is favourable to us. Two sub-elements fall short of the model wording but are not material deviations here: the notice periods in 12.2(a)(i) are redacted ([***]) and so cannot be confirmed against the 30-day preferred figure, and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts — a concept with limited application to a milestone/profit-share collaboration rather than a prepaid subscription. We should confirm on the unredacted execution version that the convenience notice period is no longer than 90 days; subject to that, the clause sits at or above the preferred position and requires no redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-ccbeabb2","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"FINANCIAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Section 9.9 is the only audit right that binds us on payments/records (Section 6.9 runs in our favour, auditing RevMed and its subcontractors). It contains every material protection the playbook seeks: a mutual and reciprocal right, a fixed minimum prior-notice period, a per-Calendar-Year frequency cap, a defined look-back with waiver of older periods, an independent auditor of international prominence subject to our reasonable acceptance, scope limited to verifying financial reports and payments, an express bar on disclosing our Confidential Information to RevMed beyond the discrepancy report (9.9(b)), and cost borne by the auditing Party unless an underpayment exceeds a stated percentage threshold (9.9(c)). There is no right of remote or direct access to our systems — the auditor reviews books and records only — so the walk-away scenario does not arise. Two minor points are noted rather than flagged: the notice period, frequency, look-back and underpayment percentage are redacted as [***], so they cannot be confirmed against the preferred 30 days / once per 12 months / 5% (or the fallback 15 days / 10%) figures; and the \"unless for cause\" carve-out to the frequency cap is a customary exception rather than an unlimited-audit right. Overall the clause sits at or above the fallback on its material terms, so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-d7c648ae","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Governing law meets our preferred position: Section 15.5 (and Section 5 of the side Letter, p0671) applies New York law with no conflict-of-laws reference. On forum, Section 15.6(a) sends Disputes to mandatory arbitration administered by JAMS under its domestic Comprehensive Arbitration Rules in English, with judgment enterable in any court having jurisdiction; patent/trademark scope and validity disputes go to the courts of the granting country (15.6(h)) and either Party may seek interim or equitable relief from a court (15.6(j)). This is a domestic, mutually binding US arbitration mechanism, not the foreign arbitration or foreign-venue outcome the rule treats as walk-away, and it applies symmetrically to both parties. The only sub-element short of the preferred wording is the absence of an express submission to the state and federal courts in New York County; that is noted rather than flagged. Note for the file: the arbitration seat in Section 15.6(a) is redacted (\"arbitration in [***]\"); we should confirm on execution that the seat is New York (or another accepted US location), since a seat outside the accepted list would change this assessment.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-95f07bea","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"FINANCIAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Document-wide searches for MFN formulations (\"most favored/favoured\", \"no less favorable\", \"at least as favo\", \"best terms\", \"comparable terms\", \"preferential\", \"match\") returned no hits, and a full read of Article IX (Financial Provisions) shows the economics — upfront, capped milestones ($520M), tiered royalties with defined reductions/floor, and the 50/50 U.S. profit/loss share — are fixed figures with no obligation on Sanofi to extend RevMed terms no less favourable than those given to any Third Party or to match a third-party offer. This meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on the Customer), so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-f14ab892","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"COMMERCIALIZATION","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall payment or volume cap on Sanofi. Searches for \"minimum\", \"shortfall\" and purchase-commitment language return nothing applicable: the only volume-related mechanics are the Commercialization Plan forecasts, which are expressly \"non-binding\" (p0370, p0373, and p0371), and Section 7.3 (p0360) merely contemplates a future supply agreement to be negotiated in good faith on commercially reasonable terms without any committed volumes. Sanofi also retains sole control of Commercialization, ordering, pricing and distribution (p0363, p0375). This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; payment tied only to actual supply/sales). Diligence/Commercially Reasonable Efforts obligations are addressed under a separate rule and are not double-flagged here. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-0b307c9e","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13.3 Covenants by RevMed. RevMed covenants to Sanofi that:","rationale":"Searches for the standard triggers (\"solicit\", \"hire\", \"induce\", \"recruit\", \"employ or engage\", \"personnel\") return no restrictive covenant on hiring: the only hits are a governance reference to \"solicited input\", the FTE definition, confidentiality recipients, debarment/inventor-assignment covenants and indemnity party lists. The covenant provisions (Sections 13.3 and 13.4, including the mutual covenants) contain no non-solicitation or no-hire undertaking, and no such covenant appears in the General Provisions. Sanofi is therefore free to solicit or hire RevMed personnel, which matches the preferred position (no non-solicit on the Customer); nothing to redline, and the absence benefits us so no \"missing\" finding is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-8c532d83","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"The RENEWAL rule is not implicated by this agreement, and nothing in it triggers the fallback or walk-away tests. Section 12.1 sets a single, self-executing term that runs until expiry of Sanofi's payment obligations under Article IX / the Profit/Loss Share Agreement; there is no automatic renewal, no renewal term, and no non-renewal notice window. Searches for \"automatically renew\", \"unless either Party gives notice\", \"renewal term\", \"successive\", and price-uplift language return no hits — the only \"renewal\"/\"non-renewal\" references are patent prosecution renewals (p0098) and insurance non-renewal notice (p0603), neither of which is a term-extension mechanic. Consequently there is no notice window to compute (so the >90-day walk-away and >60-day fallback thresholds cannot be breached), no multi-year auto-renewal, and no renewal-linked price increase to cap.\n\nThe rule's underlying concerns — easy exit and predictable renewal pricing — are already satisfied in our favour: under Section 12.2(a)(i) Sanofi may terminate for convenience in its entirety or on a country-by-country / Product-by-Product basis on written notice, plus additional Sanofi termination rights for RevMed's change of control (12.2(a)(ii)) and for safety (12.2(a)(iii)). Exit is therefore unilateral and at our discretion rather than trapped behind a renewal notice deadline.\n\nThis is treated as inapplicable rather than \"missing\": a usable term clause exists, and importing an auto-renewal-plus-opt-out construct into a biopharma collaboration and licence structured around Royalty Term expiry (p0395) would not benefit us — it would add an extension mechanic where none is wanted. No redline proposed, consistent with the instruction not to flag provisions that favour our party.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-06375757","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIALITY; PUBLICATION","rationale":"The Agreement contains a full exit/transition architecture, so no insert is needed. Section 11.6 (surviving under Section 12.4) is a mutual return/destruction-and-written-certification mechanic triggered on termination only on a party's written request, with express carve-outs allowing retention of information needed for continuing rights and obligations plus archival copies — so there is no \"immediate deletion / no data return\" walk-away risk against us, and on expiry our licences become perpetual and fully paid up (12.3(b)). {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Collaborative Research, Development and Commercialization Agreement

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Scope:** Playbook review of the Collaborative Research, Development and Commercialization Agreement. Findings below are drawn solely from the verified review record.

---

## 1. Executive summary

This agreement reviews well from our side. Of the eighteen playbook rules tested, seventeen are compliant — either at or above our preferred position — and one records a deviation (limitation of liability). Notably, no walk-away trigger is present anywhere in the document.

The commercial architecture is materially favourable to us as the exploiting licensee. We hold an exclusive licence with affiliate, sublicence and subcontractor reach (§ 3.1, § 3.4), a unilateral termination-for-convenience right exercisable in whole or country-by-country / Product-by-Product with no early-termination fee (§ 12.2(a)(i)), an uncapped counterparty indemnity carved out of the liability limitation (§§ 14.1, 14.3, 14.5), free assignment to Affiliates and to an M&A successor without consent (§ 15.2), and New York governing law with domestic JAMS arbitration (§§ 15.5, 15.6). The agreement imposes no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, minimum-purchase or liquidated-damages obligation on us, and Commercialization forecasts are expressly non-binding.

The single deviation is the absence of any aggregate monetary cap in § 14.5, which is a mutual waiver of indirect and consequential damages only. Direct-damages exposure is therefore unlimited for both parties and the clause fails the fallback on the "cap exists" term. Because that finding did not clear verification, we recommend re-verifying it against the execution text before issuing the redline.

A secondary workstream is diligence rather than negotiation: several material figures are redacted as `[***]` (convenience notice period, audit notice/frequency/look-back/underpayment threshold, arbitration seat, transition windows, the "Competing Product" definition, and part of § 10.1(a)). These do not change our current assessment but must be confirmed on the unredacted execution version.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (§§ 14.1, 14.3, 14.5, 14.6) | Counterparty indemnity covers negligence/willful misconduct, warranty breach and breach of obligations; uncapped via § 14.5 carve-out — better than the fallback super-cap. No standalone allegation-based IP indemnity and a knowledge-qualified non-infringement warranty are noted only. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | Intellectual Property Rights (Art. X; §§ 3.1, 3.5, 6.2) | Inventorship-based ownership, no assignment of our IP; joint technology carries an unrestricted right to exploit and licence without accounting or consent, so the joint-ownership walk-away does not arise. § 10.1(a) partly redacted. |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | General Provisions (§ 15.2; § 12.2(a)(ii)) | We may assign to Affiliates and to an M&A successor without consent; counterparty assignment requires our consent, with Acquiror-Family firewall conditions. No counterparty termination or re-pricing right on our change of control. |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | License (Art. III; §§ 3.6, 7.1–7.3) | No exclusivity, sole-supplier or requirements obligation on us; all exclusivity runs in our favour. Co-Promotion Option and § 12.2(d) are not exclusive-dealing covenants. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | Term and Termination (§§ 12.2(a)(i), 12.3(c); §§ 9.6, 15.6(f)) | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee payable by us. Late-payment interest is mutual and statutorily capped; punitive damages are barred in arbitration. |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | License (§§ 3.1(a), 3.4, 12.2, 12.3) | Exclusive licence, not revocable at the counterparty's discretion; extends to Affiliates, sublicensees and subcontractors; becomes perpetual and royalty-free on expiration. Consent for sublicensing substantially all US rights noted only. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Term and Termination (§ 12.2(d); §§ 3.8, 13.3–13.4, 15.2) | No restrictive covenant binds us; "Field" is any and all uses. § 12.2(d) creates a termination right only, defeasible by our written election, with no post-term restraint. "Competing Product" definition is redacted. |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | Term and Termination (§§ 12.1, 12.2, 12.3(c)) | Unilateral convenience right for us, including partial termination; counterparty has cause-based rights only. Notice period redacted — confirm it is no longer than 90 days. |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Financial Provisions (§ 9.9) | Mutual, notice-based, frequency-capped, defined look-back, independent auditor subject to our acceptance, records-only (no systems access), auditor-pays default. Thresholds redacted. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions (§§ 15.5, 15.6) | New York law with no conflicts reference; mutual JAMS domestic arbitration in English, with court routes for patent validity and interim relief. Arbitration seat is redacted — confirm it is New York or another accepted US location. |
| 11 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | Financial Provisions (Art. IX) | No MFN, matching or "no less favourable" obligation; economics are fixed figures. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Commercialization (§§ 7.3, 8.x) | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume cap; forecasts expressly non-binding; we retain sole control of ordering, pricing and distribution. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 13.3 Covenants by RevMed (and § 13.4) | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant anywhere in the agreement; the absence benefits us. |
| 14 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant (rule not implicated) | Term and Termination (§§ 12.1, 12.2(a)) | Single self-executing term keyed to expiry of payment obligations; no renewal term, notice window or renewal-linked uplift. Exit is unilateral at our discretion. |
| 15 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Compliant | Confidentiality; Publication (§ 11.6; §§ 12.3(b)–(e), 12.4) | Mutual return/destruction on written request with retention carve-outs; defined transition assistance and regulatory/clinical data transfer; our licences go perpetual on expiry. Post-termination windows redacted. |
| 16 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | Research (§ 4.2(b); Art. XIII) | Substantive performance standard (GMP/GLP/GCP), extensive title, non-infringement and compliance warranties, with a JRDC cure process, step-in rights, indemnity and termination remedies. § 13.5 disclaimer expressly preserves Art. XIII, so no "AS IS" exposure. Warranties given as of the Execution Date, with a closing bring-down. |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant (at fallback) | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (§ 14.6) | Mutual insurance covenant including product liability, certificates on request, and one-way pre-cancellation notice to us; self-insurance permitted for us and insurance is not a cap on indemnity. Limits set by market practice rather than stated figures. |
| 18 | Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** (verification: fail — re-verify before issuing) | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (§ 14.5) | § 14.5 waives indirect, consequential, incidental and punitive damages and lost profits, with carve-outs for §§ 14.1/14.2 indemnification and Art. X/XI breaches, but contains no aggregate monetary cap anywhere in the agreement, so direct-damages exposure is unlimited for both parties and the fallback is not met. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

None. No finding in this review reached walk-away territory:

- **Indemnity** is present, mutual in structure and uncapped in our favour (§§ 14.1, 14.5).
- **IP** is not assigned away, and joint ownership carries an unrestricted right to exploit and licence without accounting or consent — the joint-ownership walk-away does not apply (§ 10.1(b)).
- **Audit** is records-only, with no remote or direct systems access (§ 9.9).
- **Warranty** is not disclaimed on an "AS IS" basis; § 13.5 preserves Article XIII in full.
- **Data return** is on request with retention carve-outs, not immediate deletion, and our licences become perpetual on expiry (§§ 11.6, 12.3(b)).
- **Forum** is domestic US arbitration under JAMS, not foreign arbitration or a foreign venue (§ 15.6(a)).

Two redactions are the only items capable of changing that conclusion, and both are watch-items rather than current issues: the arbitration **seat** in § 15.6(a) (a seat outside the accepted US list would change our governing-law/venue assessment) and the definition of **"Competing Product"** (whose breadth we cannot presently verify).

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-verify the § 14.5 finding.** This is our only deviation and it did not clear verification. Before any redline goes out, confirm against the execution text that no aggregate liability cap appears elsewhere in the agreement or in the side Letter or Profit/Loss Share Agreement.
2. **If confirmed, propose the § 14.5 repair.** Keep the existing waiver and carve-out sentence intact; extend the carve-outs to data protection, security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud as a defined set of "Excluded Claims"; and add one sentence imposing a **mutual** cap at the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, confirming that our payment obligations are not damages. Note that the current uncapped position cuts both ways, so we should take a commercial view on whether we prefer symmetry or the status quo before tabling this.
3. **Clear the redactions on the unredacted execution version.** Specifically: the § 12.2(a)(i) convenience notice period (confirm no longer than 90 days); the § 9.9 audit notice period, frequency, look-back and underpayment percentage (preferred 30 days / once per 12 months / 5%; fallback 15 days / 10%); the § 15.6(a) arbitration seat (confirm New York or another accepted US location); the § 12.3(c)(vi) transition time periods; the "Competing Product" definition; and the redacted portion of § 10.1(a) on inventorship allocation.
4. **Confirm commercially, not legally.** The § 12.3(c)(vi) effort and duration limits on transition assistance and the § 14.6 insurance limits (set by market practice rather than stated figures) are business calls for the deal team, not playbook breaches.
5. **No other redlines.** The remaining sixteen compliant findings require no amendment, and several provisions run in our favour and should not be disturbed — in particular our self-insurance right and the non-capping of indemnity in § 14.6, the post-termination royalties payable to us under § 12.3(c)(ii)(C), and the absence of any non-solicit, MFN or minimum-commitment obligation.

*This memo relies solely on the findings supplied and does not extend to provisions outside the rules tested.*"}
